description:
We are HamTerra, a team passionate about using technology, Earth observation, and data-driven innovation to address real-world environmental challenges.

I'm Hamdani, a DevOps Engineer and AI/ML Engineer with interests in artificial intelligence, geospatial technology, satellite imagery, and environmental monitoring. My experience includes building machine learning applications, working with computer vision models, developing cloud-based systems, and analysing geospatial data.
summary:
Eco-Sentinel Ghana is a satellite-based environmental monitoring platform designed to help researchers and environmental organizations observe and understand changes in mining-affected landscapes in Ghana.

Developed under the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge, the platform brings together satellite observations, vegetation indices such as the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and weather information to examine environmental trends over time. Users can explore monitoring areas on an interactive map, view satellite observations, analyse vegetation trends, and compare observations across different dates.

Using Earth observation data, Eco-Sentinel aims to make environmental changes easier to visualise and investigate, helping researchers identify areas that may warrant further attention.

By making geospatial and environmental information more accessible, Eco-Sentinel Ghana supports evidence-based environmental monitoring and contributes to efforts to better understand the impacts of mining on Ghana's landscapes.
details:
Eco-Sentinel Ghana is a working satellite-based environmental monitoring platform developed to help researchers and environmental organisations observe and investigate changes in mining-affected landscapes in Ghana.

The platform allows users to explore geographical monitoring areas, retrieve satellite observations, examine vegetation conditions using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), compare observations across different dates, and view environmental trends through maps and data visualisations. It also incorporates weather information to provide additional context when interpreting observed changes.

Our workflow combines satellite observation retrieval, geospatial processing, vegetation-index analysis, historical comparison, and interactive visualisation. We tested the platform using a monitoring area around Prestea, Ghana, and analysed Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 observations across multiple dates.

Eco-Sentinel's main benefit is making satellite-derived environmental information easier to explore and interpret. It can support environmental research, monitoring activities, and evidence-based investigation by helping users identify changes that may require further attention.

The project's intended impact is to improve access to Earth observation insights and support a better understanding of environmental changes in mining-affected areas. Its creative approach brings satellite observations, vegetation analysis, weather context, and geospatial visualisation together in one accessible platform.

The project uses Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, geospatial and data-analysis libraries, Docker, and satellite-data APIs. The prototype was developed and tested locally, with deployment underway.

An important consideration is that NDVI changes do not independently prove illegal mining or establish the cause of environmental change. Seasonal vegetation patterns, rainfall, cloud conditions, and differences between satellite observations must also be considered. Eco-Sentinel presents information to support investigation rather than making unsupported conclusions.
